wormald.shelfmark: York Gospels (York Minster) — Wormald gives no shelfmark; Ker, Catalogue no. 402
wormald.wormald_date: Gospel-book last part of s. x, with a page supplied by Eadwig Basan (s. xi, 2nd–3rd decade); Cnut's letter and the three Wulfstan tracts copied 1020×1023 (Table 4.1 's. x/xi – 1020x1023', p. 164; pp. 195, 197)
wormald.wormald_origin: York: at York from Wulfstan's time to the present (bar a seventeenth-century interlude) (p. 195). Wormald guesses it was finished at Christ Church, Canterbury (a page supplied by Eadwig Basan) for presentation to Wulfstan when he consecrated Archbishop Æthelnoth in 1020 (p. 195). Used for oaths of office of cathedral clergy; kept in the cathedral treasury with other jewelled books (pp. 195, 197).
wormald.laws: Cn 1020 (sole surviving copy), in the same hand as and immediately after the three Wulfstan tracts, on ff. 158–60 (Wormald gives no separate folio)
wormald.other_contents: Gospel-book; property memoranda on York estates (ff. 156v–157r); a new gathering (ff. 158–61) with three Wulfstan tracts (a 'Sermo Lupi' on Christian duties, 'On Heathenism', 'On Christianity'; Napier LIX–LXI), each glossed by Wulfstan's hand, then Cnut's letter in the same hand; lists of church treasures and of Archbishop Ælfric's festermen (f. 161r–v); oath formulae (pp. 195–6).
wormald.overview: A late tenth-century Gospel-book, perhaps completed at Canterbury and at York from Wulfstan's time onward, to which were added York estate records, three law-like Wulfstan tracts glossed by the archbishop, and, written by the scribe of the tracts, the sole surviving text of Cnut's 1019×20 letter to the English. Because the copying took place before Wulfstan's death in May 1023, the letter is uniquely close to its issue. The laying out of letter and tracts alike as clauses shows how little Wulfstan distinguished law from homily, and its placing in a holy book shows royal law being enshrined beside God's.
wormald.liebermann_superseded: Liebermann dated the gospel book c. 1025 and the homilies and letter c. 1030–70; Wormald shows the book is of the late tenth century and that the tracts and the letter were copied before Wulfstan's death in May 1023, since his hand glosses them (pp. 195, 197).
wormald.doubts: GUIDE: Liebermann's dates (c. 1025; homilies c. 1030–70) are superseded. Wormald (p. 195 n. 137) notes the MS 'has no Liebermann siglum as such'; the guide uses 'York'. Wormald gives no shelfmark; guide's 'York, Minster Library, Add. 1' not confirmed or contradicted here. Folio for Cn 1020 inferred: additions on ff. 158–60 'first three leaves' of the new gathering, letter after the tracts. Ker, before rebinding, took ff. 156–61 as one quire (p. 196). The guide says the letter is 'on a flyleaf'; Wormald places it in the added gathering.
verify_notes: origin/overview: Canterbury finishing is Wormald’s guess, not ‘probably’ (p. 195).
laws: folio ‘f. 160’ was an inference; replaced with ff. 158–60 as Wormald gives.

A late tenth-century Gospel-book, perhaps completed at Canterbury and at York from Wulfstan's time onward, to which were added York estate records, three law-like Wulfstan tracts glossed by the archbishop, and, written by the scribe of the tracts, the sole surviving text of Cnut's 1019×20 letter to the English. Because the copying took place before Wulfstan's death in May 1023, the letter is uniquely close to its issue. The laying out of letter and tracts alike as clauses shows how little Wulfstan distinguished law from homily, and its placing in a holy book shows royal law being enshrined beside God's.

Liebermann dated the gospel book c. 1025 and the homilies and letter c. 1030–70; Wormald shows the book is of the late tenth century and that the tracts and the letter were copied before Wulfstan's death in May 1023, since his hand glosses them (pp. 195, 197).
